after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{1+5x}+\frac{1}{1-5x})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
after.worked_solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{1+5x}+\frac{1}{1-5x})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{1+5x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{1-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+5x|-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-5x|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{1+5x}{1-5x}|+\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|\frac{1+5x}{1-5x}|)\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{1+5x}+\frac{1}{1-5x})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{1+5x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{1-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+5x|-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-5x|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{1+5x}{1-5x}|+\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|\frac{1+5x}{1-5x}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.

after.problem: Calculate $\int \frac{1}{7-x}\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
after.worked_solution:
First, let $u=7-x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{7-x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (-1)\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the above by writing $C=-\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ for another arbitrary constant $K,$ and then we can combine the two terms using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-x|+C & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-x|-\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =-(\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|7-x|)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we finally conclude that

$$
\int \frac{1}{7-x}\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|7-x|).
$$

content.problem: Calculate $\int \frac{1}{7-x}\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
content.worked_solution:
First, let $u=7-x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{7-x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (-1)\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the above by writing $C=-\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ for another arbitrary constant $K,$ and then we can combine the two terms using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-x|+C & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-x|-\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =-(\operatorname{ln}⁡|7-x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|7-x|)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we finally conclude that

$$
\int \frac{1}{7-x}\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|7-x|).
$$

decision.explanation: Integrating term by term gives (1/4)ln|4x−5|−(1/4)ln|1−4x|+C. Combining logarithms and absorbing C into K>0 gives (1/4)ln(K|(4x−5)/(1−4x)|), which is option b.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{4x-5}+\frac{1}{1-4x})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
after.worked_solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{4x-5}+\frac{1}{1-4x})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{4x-5}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{1-4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x-5|-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-4x|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{4x-5}{1-4x}|+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|\frac{4x-5}{1-4x}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.

content.problem: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{4x-5}+\frac{1}{1-4x})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
content.worked_solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{4x-5}+\frac{1}{1-4x})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{4x-5}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{1-4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x-5|-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-4x|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{4x-5}{1-4x}|+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|\frac{4x-5}{1-4x}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.

12ln⁡(K|2x+12x−1|)
b

decision.explanation: Each denominator has derivative 2, so the integral is (1/2)ln|2x+1|+(1/2)ln|2x−1|+C. Adding logarithms gives (1/2)ln(K|(2x+1)(2x−1)|), with K>0 absorbing the constant.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{2x+1}+\frac{1}{2x-1})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
after.worked_solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{2x+1}+\frac{1}{2x-1})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{2x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-1|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|(2x+1)(2x-1)|+\frac{1}{2}\text{ }\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|(2x+1)(2x-1)|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.

content.problem: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{2x+1}+\frac{1}{2x-1})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
content.worked_solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{2x+1}+\frac{1}{2x-1})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{2x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-1|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|(2x+1)(2x-1)|+\frac{1}{2}\text{ }\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|(2x+1)(2x-1)|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.

after.problem: Calculate $\int \frac{1}{2x+3}\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
after.worked_solution:
First, let $u=2x+3.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$
